@@U04027@@
And once beyond the city gates, the merchant and wayfarer were as good as dead! Audacity and daring were the orders of the day. Life meant not lowering your guard for a second. And so it went.

@@U04029@@
It went, it hobbled, fell and got up again, then took a tumble and rolled into a great heap.

@@U04031@@
And no one dared complain, for everyone now had the right and the will to be important, and they insisted on it. Even a nonentity was considered a somebody. At last the best and soundest among them had had enough, and rose up in force to declare that the man who could bring them peace would rule as emperor. “The Emperor,” they said, “neither can nor wants to! Let us elect us a new Emperor who will breathe new life into the empire, secure the rights of every man, and join righteousness with peace in a new-made world!”

@@U04033@@
I hear a priestly ring in that!

@@U04035@@
Ah, yes, indeed! Priests! Securing their well-stuffed bellies. After all, they had more to lose than anyone. The insurrection grew, they blessed the rebels, and our Emperor, whom we so lately entertained, comes here to fight— perhaps his last battle.
translation:
@@U04027@@
一旦出了城门，商人和行人就等于死了！大胆和大胆是当时的潮流。生活意味着一刻都不能放松警惕。事情就这样过去了。

@@U04029@@
它走了，一瘸一拐，摔倒了，又爬起来，然后摔了一跤，滚成了一大堆。

@@U04031@@
没有人敢抱怨，因为现在每个人都有权利和意愿变得重要，而且他们坚持这样做。即使是一个无名小卒也被认为是一个重要人物。最后，他们中最优秀、最健全的人受够了，纷纷起来宣布，能给他们带来和平的人将成为皇帝。 “皇帝，”他们说，“既不能也不想！让我们选出一位新皇帝，他将为帝国注入新的活力，保障每个人的权利，并在新世界中将正义与和平结合起来！”

@@U04033@@
我听到里面有牧师的铃声！

@@U04035@@
啊，是的，确实如此！牧师们！确保他们的肚子饱饱的。毕竟，他们的损失比任何人都多。叛乱愈演愈烈，他们祝福叛乱者，而我们最近接待的皇帝来到这里参加战斗——也许是他的最后一场战斗。
